title: Formulas, calculation steps, and references / 公式、计算过程与参考文献
text: calculate() sample_size_calculator() return sample_size_result object. Printing displays study design, required sample size, four report components. Assigning result variable stores ; print(res) entering res R console displays report. calculate() 和 sample_size_calculator() 返回 sample_size_result 对象。 默认打印会显示研究设计、所需样本量，以及以下四项内容。赋值仅保存结果； 输入对象名称或调用 print(res) 即可查看完整输出。 following example runs page built. calculation process shows normal approximation 35.32 per arm, followed noncentral t power calculation rounding 37 per arm (74 total). Intermediate calculations rounding depend chosen method. 以下示例在构建页面时实际运行。计算过程先列出每组约 35.32 人的正态近似， 再说明非中心 t 分布效能求解和取整，最终为每组 37 人、合计 74 人。 不同设计采用的中间计算与取整规则有所不同。
code: res <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) print(res) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

code: summary(res) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Summary #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> ── Study Design #> • Type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Design: "rct" #> • Task: "test" | Outcome: "mean" #>  #> ── Parameters #> • mean1: 10 #> • mean2: 12 #> • sd: 3 #> • alpha: 0.05 #> • power: 0.8 #>  #> ── Sample Size Results #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #>  #> ── Formula #> Plain text: #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> LaTeX: #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #>  #> ── Calculation Process #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #>  #> ── Reference #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── legacy_res <- sample_size_calculator(   "twoProportions", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.70 ) print(legacy_res) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent proportions" #> • Sample size per group: 121 #> • Total sample size: 242 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_a/2 * sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_b * sqrt(p1*(1-p1)+p2*(1-p2)))^2 / #> (p1-p2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: p1 = p2 vs H1: p1 != p2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute pooled proportion: p_bar = (p1 + p2) / 2 = (0.85 + 0.70) / 2 #> = 0.775. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute Fleiss formula numerator components: #> Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) = 1.1575; Z_beta*sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) = #> 0.4889. #> • Step 5: Calculate unrounded sample size per group: n = (1.1575 + 0.4889)^2 / #> (0.85 - 0.70)^2 = 120.47. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 121 per group, total sample size N = 242. #> Reference: #> Primary (formula as implemented, without continuity correction): Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, A., & Ury, H. K. (1980). A simple approximation for calculating sample sizes for comparing independent proportions. Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. #>  #> With continuity correction: Casagrande, J. T., Pike, M. C., & Smith, P. G. (1978). An improved approximate formula for calculating sample sizes for comparing two binomial distributions. Biometrics, 34(3), 483-494. #>  #> Book: Fleiss, J. L., Levin, B., & Paik, M. C. (2003). Statistical methods for rates and proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

what: Introduction: The Lifeblood of Clinical Research
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: clinical investigators, calculating sample size often critical step preparing grant proposals IRB submissions. Underpowered trials risk false-negative findings (\(P > 0.05\)), wasting research grants patient effort. Conversely, overpowered trials waste resources expose unnecessary subjects experimental risks. sampleSizeCalc package provides support 42 specific clinical scenarios. Default printed results include plain-text formula, LaTeX source, calculation process, literature references, parameter roles available. Every executable example runs site built, output comes package.

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: \(\alpha\) (Type Error / False Positive): probability declaring treatment effective truly — “probability convicting innocent drug” (conventionally 0.05). \(\text{Power} = 1 - \beta\) (True Positive Detection): probability catching true effect exists — “probability catching real culprit” (routinely 0.80 0.90). Continuous vs. Binary Endpoints: Continuous measures numerical values (systolic BP drop mmHg, fasting glucose mmol/L); binary measures event status (eradicated vs. , cured vs. ). Two-Sided vs. One-Sided: Two-sided tests differences either direction (classical RCTs); one-sided tests non-inferiority directional superiority. Dropout Rate (\(d\)): Inflation formula \(N_{\text{screen}} = \lceil N / (1 - d) \rceil\).

what: Unified Syntax: The Three-Axis Function calculate()
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: \[\texttt{calculate(design, task, outcome, ...)}\] Axis 1 design: type study? ("rct", "paired", "cohort", "caseControl", "diagAccuracy", "diagAUC", "singleArmPhaseII", "bioequivalence", "clusterRCT", …) Axis 2 task: scientific question? ("test" hypothesis testing, "estimate" CI precision, "noninferiority", "superiority", "equivalence") Axis 3 outcome: endpoint measured? ("mean", "proportion", "survival", "auc", "rate", "ordinal", "lr", "correlation", "events") Printing result shows formula plain text LaTeX, calculation process, references. summary() also lists inputs, design axes, recorded adjustments.

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: cardiology group runs phase-III antihypertensive trial new ACE-inhibitor vs. placebo. phase-II data showed mean systolic BP reduction 10 mmHg placebo 12 mmHg new drug, pooled SD 3 mmHg. Two-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\), power 80%. Formula: \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2\] Chow, Shao, Wang & Lokhnygina (2017), Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.), CRC Press. Output: 37 patients per arm, 74 total. calculation process shows normal approximation (35.32 per arm), explains noncentral t power calculation used stats::power.t.test() rounding 37.
code: res_1_1 <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Gastroenterology trial H. pylori eradication: 14-day bismuth quadruple therapy expected eradicate 85% infections vs. 70% standard triple therapy. Two-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\), power 80%. Formula (Fleiss asymptotic): \[n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1)+p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_2)^2}\] Fleiss, Tytun & Ury (1980), Biometrics 36(2), 343-346. Output: 121 patients per arm, 242 total.
code: res_1_2 <- calculate("rct", "test", "proportion", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.70, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_2) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent proportions" #> • Sample size per group: 121 #> • Total sample size: 242 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_a/2 * sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_b * sqrt(p1*(1-p1)+p2*(1-p2)))^2 / #> (p1-p2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: p1 = p2 vs H1: p1 != p2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute pooled proportion: p_bar = (p1 + p2) / 2 = (0.85 + 0.70) / 2 #> = 0.775. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute Fleiss formula numerator components: #> Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) = 1.1575; Z_beta*sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) = #> 0.4889. #> • Step 5: Calculate unrounded sample size per group: n = (1.1575 + 0.4889)^2 / #> (0.85 - 0.70)^2 = 120.47. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 121 per group, total sample size N = 242. #> Reference: #> Primary (formula as implemented, without continuity correction): Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, A., & Ury, H. K. (1980). A simple approximation for calculating sample sizes for comparing independent proportions. Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. #>  #> With continuity correction: Casagrande, J. T., Pike, M. C., & Smith, P. G. (1978). An improved approximate formula for calculating sample sizes for comparing two binomial distributions. Biometrics, 34(3), 483-494. #>  #> Book: Fleiss, J. L., Levin, B., & Paik, M. C. (2003). Statistical methods for rates and proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Oncology trial first-line immunotherapy vs. chemotherapy non-small-cell lung cancer; anticipated hazard ratio HR = 0.70 1:1 allocation. many deaths/progressions must accrue? Formula (Schoenfeld): \[E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1 - p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}\] Schoenfeld (1983), Biometrics 39(2), 499-503. Output: Exactly 247 primary events (deaths/progressions) required.
code: res_1_3 <- calculate("rct", "test", "survival", hr = 0.70, pE = 0.50, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Survival (log-rank)" #> • Events needed: 247 #> Formula (plain text): #> `E = (Z_a/2 + Z_b)^2 / (pE*(1-pE)*log(HR)^2)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State survival parameters: Hazard Ratio HR = 0.70, experimental arm #> allocation pE = 0.50 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute log hazard ratio: ln(HR) = ln(0.70) = -0.3567. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Apply Schoenfeld formula: E = (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [pE * (1 - #> pE) * (ln HR)^2] = (1.96 + 0.8416)^2 / [0.50 * 0.50 * (-0.3567)^2] = 246.79. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target events needed E = 247. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schoenfeld, D. A. (1983). Sample-size formula for the proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. #>  #> Extensions: #> - Hsieh, F. Y., & Lavori, P. W. (2000). Sample-size calculations for the Cox proportional hazards regression model with nonbinary covariates. Controlled Clinical Trials, 21(6), 552-560. #> - Rubinstein, L. V., Gail, M. H., & Santner, T. J. (1981). Planning the duration of a comparative clinical trial with loss to follow-up and a period of continued observation. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 34(9-10), 469-479. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: domestic generic antidiabetic must show worse originator prespecified margin. 0-30 neuropathy symptom score improvement expected 10 vs. 9.5 points (SD = 3); margin \(\Delta = 1.0\). One-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\). Formula: \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2\] Chow et al. (2017), Chapter 4. Output: 50 per arm, 100 total.
code: res_1_4 <- calculate("rct", "noninferiority", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 9.5, sd = 3, margin = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_4) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 50 #> • Total sample size: 100 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2+margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= -margin vs H1: mu1 #> - mu2 > -margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 + margin = 10 - 9.50 + 1 = #> 1.50; SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta = #> 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 / #> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * 3^2 / (1.50)^2 = 49.46. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 50 per group, total sample size N = 100. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: generic antibiotic must show non-inferior cure rates vs. originator: anticipated 85%, clinically acceptable margin 5% (\(\Delta = 0.05\)). One-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\). Formula: \[n = \frac{(Z_{\alpha}+Z_{\beta})^2\left[p_1(1-p_1)+p_2(1-p_2)\right]}{(p_1-p_2+\Delta)^2}\] Chow et al. (2017); Machin et al. (2018) Ch. 11. Output: 631 per arm, 1262 total.
code: res_1_5 <- calculate("rct", "noninferiority", "proportion", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.85, margin = 0.05, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_5) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (proportions)" #> • Sample size per group: 631 #> • Total sample size: 1262 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p1 = experimental-group response rate #> • p2 = active-control response rate #> • margin = non-inferiority margin Delta (one-sided alpha) #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Za+Zb)^2 * (p1q1+p2q2) / (p1-p2+margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{(Z_{\alpha}+Z_{\beta})^2\left[p_1(1-p_1)+p_2(1-p_2)\right]}{(p_1-p_2+\Delta)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: p1 - p2 <= -margin vs H1: p1 - #> p2 > -margin (margin Delta = 0.05, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = p1 - p2 + margin = 0.85 - 0.85 + 0.05 #> = 0.05. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta = #> 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * [p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2)] #> / delta_E^2 = 630.62. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 631 per group, total sample size N = 1262. #> Reference: #> Primary: Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press; Machin et al. (2018) Chapter 11 (Non-inferiority and Equivalence). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Knee osteoarthritis trial: new NSAID gel must beat active comparator WOMAC pain subscale (0-20) 1 point. Anticipated reductions: 12 vs. 10 points, SD = 3. One-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\). Formula: \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 - \Delta}\right)^2\] Chow et al. (2017). Output: 112 per arm, 224 total.
code: res_1_6 <- calculate("rct", "superiority", "mean", mean1 = 12, mean2 = 10, sd = 3, margin = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_6) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Superiority (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 112 #> • Total sample size: 224 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2-margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 - \Delta}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State superiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= margin vs H1: mu1 - #> mu2 > margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 - margin = 12 - 10 - 1 = 1; #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta = #> 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 / #> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * 3^2 / (1)^2 = 111.29. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 112 per group, total sample size N = 224. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Onychomycosis trial: complete cure rate 30% new oral antifungal vs. 20% terbinafine, sponsor requires difference exceed 5% superiority margin. Formula: \[n = \frac{(Z_{\alpha}+Z_{\beta})^2\left[p_1(1-p_1)+p_2(1-p_2)\right]}{(p_1-p_2-\Delta)^2}\] Chow et al. (2017). Output: 916 per arm, 1832 total.
code: res_1_7 <- calculate("rct", "superiority", "proportion", p1 = 0.30, p2 = 0.20, margin = 0.05, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_7) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Superiority (proportions)" #> • Sample size per group: 916 #> • Total sample size: 1832 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * (p1*(1-p1) + p2*(1-p2)) / (p1 - p2 - margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})^2[p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)]}{(p_1 - p_2 - \Delta)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State superiority hypotheses: H0: p1 - p2 <= margin vs H1: p1 - p2 > #> margin (margin Delta = 0.05, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = p1 - p2 - margin = 0.30 - 0.20 - 0.05 #> = 0.05. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta = #> 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * [p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2)] #> / delta_E^2 = (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * [0.21 + 0.16] / (0.05)^2 = 915.02. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 916 per group, total sample size N = 1832. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Two formulations levothyroxine must shown therapeutically equivalent: mean serum thyroxine 10 vs. 10.2 \(\mu\)g/dL (SD = 3), equivalence corridor \(\pm 1.0\) \(\mu\)g/dL. Formula (TOST): \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta/2})\sigma}{\Delta - |\mu_1 - \mu_2|}\right)^2\] Chow et al. (2017). Output: 241 per arm, 482 total.
code: res_1_8 <- calculate("rct", "equivalence", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 10.2, sd = 3, margin = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_8) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Equivalence (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 241 #> • Total sample size: 482 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b/2)^2*sd^2/(margin-|mean1-mean2|)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta/2})\sigma}{\Delta - |\mu_1 - \mu_2|}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State equivalence hypotheses (TOST): H0: |mu1 - mu2| >= margin vs H1: #> |mu1 - mu2| < margin (margin Delta = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Margin clearance: Delta - |mu1 - mu2| = 1 - |10 - 10.20| = 0.80; SD #> sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_(beta/2) = #> 1.2816. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_(beta/2))^2 * sigma^2 / #> (Delta - |mu1 - mu2|)^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 1.2816)^2 * 3^2 / (0.80)^2 = 240.86. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 241 per group, total sample size N = 482. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Two analgesics post-operative pain: response rates 50% vs. 52%; regulators accept equivalence within \(\pm 10\) percentage points. Formula: \[n = \frac{(Z_{\alpha}+Z_{\beta/2})^2\left[p_1(1-p_1)+p_2(1-p_2)\right]}{(\Delta-|p_1-p_2|)^2}\] Chow et al. (2017). Output: 669 per arm, 1338 total.

what: 2.5 Phase II Simon’s Optimal Two-Stage Design
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: single-arm phase-II trial new sarcoma regimen: unacceptable response rate \(p_0 = 0.10\), target \(p_1 = 0.30\). optimal design minimises expected sample size drug ineffective. Formula: exact binomial enumeration (Simon 1989). design \((r_1/n_1, r/n)\) satisfies \[\underbrace{P(X_1 \le r_1 \mid p_0)}_{\text{early stop}} + \sum_{x_1=r_1+1}^{n_1}\binom{n_1}{x_1}p_0^{x_1}(1-p_0)^{n_1-x_1}\,\underbrace{P(X_2 > r - x_1 \mid p_0)}_{\text{stage 2}} \le \alpha\] analogous expression \(p_1\) must reach target power. Simon (1989), Controlled Clinical Trials 10(1), 1-10. Output: Stage 1 enrolls 10 (stop \(\le 1\) response); Stage 2 reaches 29 (effective \(>5\) responses). Expected \(N = 15.0\).
code: res_2_5 <- calculate("singleArmPhaseII", "test", "proportion", p0 = 0.10, p1 = 0.30, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8, optimizer = "optimal") print(res_2_5) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single-arm phase II (Simon two-stage, optimal)" #> • Stage 1 sample size: 10 #> • Stage 1 futility boundary (stop if responses <= r1): 1 #> • Total sample size (both stages): 29 #> • Overall boundary (declare effective if responses > r): 5 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p0 = unacceptable response rate (null) #> • p1 = desirable response rate (alternative) #> • stage 1: stop for futility if responses <= r_stage_1 of n_stage_1 #> • overall: declare effective if responses > r_total of n_total #> Formula (plain text): #> `exact binomial: P(effective|p0) <= alpha and P(effective|p1) >= power` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$P(\text{reject } H_0 \mid p_0) \le \alpha \quad \text{and} \quad P(\text{reject } H_0 \mid p_1) \ge 1-\beta$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State phase II hypotheses: H0: p <= 0.10 (unacceptable) vs H1: p >= #> 0.30 (promising) (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Exhaustive exact binomial search under 'optimal' criterion. #> • Step 3: Stage 1: Accrue n1 = 10 patients; stop early for futility if #> responses <= r1 = 1. #> • Step 4: Stage 2: If > 1 responses observed, accrue additional 19 patients up #> to total n = 29. #> • Step 5: Final decision: Declare effective if total responses > r = 5 #> (Expected sample size under H0 = 15). #> Reference: #> Primary: Simon, R. (1989). Optimal two-stage designs for phase II clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 10(1), 1-10. #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Chapter 17 (Therapeutic Exploratory Trials). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

text: Clinical scenario: Framingham-style cohort smoking coronary heart disease: 5-year incidence 20% non-smokers vs. 30% smokers, 1:1 allocation, planning 10% loss follow-. Formula: \[n_{1} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+\frac{1}{m})\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1)+\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{m}}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}, \quad n = \frac{n_1}{1-d}\] Bhardwaj et al. (2024), J Family Med Prim Care 13(7), 2559. Output: 327 per arm, 654 total.
code: res_3_1 <- calculate("cohort", "test", "proportion", p0 = 0.20, p1 = 0.30, ratio = 1, dropout = 0.10, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_3_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cohort study (cumulative incidence, RR)" #> • Sample size per group: 327 #> • Exposed group: 327 #> • Unexposed group: 327 #> • Total sample size: 654 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p0 = unexposed-group cumulative incidence #> • p1 = exposed-group cumulative incidence #> • ratio = unexposed:exposed allocation (m) #> • effect measure: risk ratio RR (estimable in cohort designs) #> Formula (plain text): #> `n1 = [Za*sqrt((1+1/m)*pbar*(1-pbar)) + Zb*sqrt(p1q1+p0q0/m)]^2/(p1-p0)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{1} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+\frac{1}{m})\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1)+\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{m}}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify proportions: unexposed p0 = 0.20, exposed p1 = 0.30, #> allocation ratio m = 1 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Weighted average proportion: p_bar = (p1 + m*p0) / (1 + m) = 0.25. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Calculate exposed sample size: n_exposed = #> [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta*sqrt(p1*q1 + p0*q0/m)]^2 / #> (p1 - p0)^2 = 293.15. #> • Step 5: Calculate unexposed sample size: n_unexposed = m * n_exposed = 1 * #> 293.15 = 293.15. #> • Step 6: Round up before dropout inflation: ceiling(n_exposed) = 294, #> ceiling(m*n_exposed) = 294; apply dropout d = 0.10 using ceiling(n/(1-d)). #> Exposed = 327, Unexposed = 327, Total sample size N = 654. #> Reference: #> Primary: Bhardwaj et al. (2024). Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care, 13(7), 2559 (worked example: p0=0.20, p1=0.30, m=1 -> 293/group). #>  #>  Also: Schlesselman, J. J. (1982). Case-Control Studies. Oxford University Press (cohort/case-control shared formula, roles swapped); Machin et al. (2018) Ch.3. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Occupational epidemiology: workers exposed solvent develop disease 0.20 events per person-year vs. 0.10 unexposed workers; 1:1 person-time allocation. Formula: \[T_{0} = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2}+Z_{\beta})^2(\lambda_1/r+\lambda_0)}{(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)^2}, \quad T_1 = r \cdot T_0\] Machin et al. (2018), Chapter 6. Output: 236 person-time units per group (71 expected events).
code: res_3_2 <- calculate("cohort", "test", "rate", rate0 = 0.10, rate1 = 0.20, ratio = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_3_2) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cohort study (incidence rate ratio, person-time)" #> • Person-time, exposed group: 236 #> • Person-time, unexposed group: 236 #> • Expected events: 71 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • rate0 = unexposed-group incidence rate (events per person-time) #> • rate1 = exposed-group incidence rate #> • ratio = unexposed:exposed person-time ratio #> • effect measure: incidence rate ratio IRR #> • person-time = total follow-up time; for fixed duration FT, subjects needed = #> person-time / FT #> Formula (plain text): #> `T0 = (Za/2+Zb)^2 * (l1/r + l0) / (l1-l0)^2 ; T1 = r*T0` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$T_{0} = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2}+Z_{\beta})^2(\lambda_1/r+\lambda_0)}{(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)^2}, \quad T_1 = r \cdot T_0$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify incidence rates: unexposed lambda0 = 0.10, exposed lambda1 = #> 0.20, person-time ratio r = 1. #> • Step 2: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 3: Calculate required person-time for unexposed group: T0 = (Z_(alpha/2) #> + Z_beta)^2 * (lambda1/r + lambda0) / (lambda1 - lambda0)^2 = 235.47. #> • Step 4: Calculate required person-time for exposed group: T1 = r * T0 = 1 * #> 235.47 = 235.47. #> • Step 5: Expected events: E = lambda0 * T0 + lambda1 * T1 = 71. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: Person-time unexposed = 236, Person-time exposed #> = 236. #> Reference: #> Primary: Machin, D., Campbell, M. J., Tan, S. B., & Tan, S. H. (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.). Wiley. Chapter 6 (Rate Outcomes). #>  #>  Also: Breslow, N. E., & Day, N. E. (1987). Statistical Methods in Cancer Research Vol. II. IARC (person-time rate comparison). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Hospital-based case-control study late-night screen exposure myocardial infarction: 30% controls exposed, anticipated = 2.0, 1 control per case. Formula (Schlesselman): \[n_{cases} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+1/m)\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_0(1-p_0)/m}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}\] Schlesselman (1982), Case-Control Studies, Oxford University Press. Output: 141 cases, 141 controls (282 total).
code: res_3_3 <- calculate("caseControl", p0 = 0.30, OR = 2.0, m = 1, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_3_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Case-control" #> • Cases needed: 141 #> • Controls needed: 141 #> • Total subjects: 282 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n_cases = [Z_alpha/2 * sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta * sqrt(p1*(1-p1) #> + p0*(1-p0)/m)]^2 / (p1 - p0)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+1/m)\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_0(1-p_0)/m}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Compute case exposure rate from Odds Ratio: p1 = (OR * p0) / (1 - p0 #> + OR * p0) = (2 * 0.30) / (1 - 0.30 + 2 * 0.30) = 0.4615. #> • Step 2: Weighted average exposure (matching ratio m = 1): p_bar = (p1 + m*p0) #> / (1 + m) = 0.3808. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Schlesselman formula for cases: n_cases = #> [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta*sqrt(p1*(1-p1) + #> p0*(1-p0)/m)]^2 / (p1 - p0)^2 = 140.66. #> • Step 5: Calculate controls needed: n_controls = m * n_cases = 1 * 140.66 = #> 140.66. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: Cases needed = 141, Controls needed = 141, Total #> subjects = 282. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schlesselman, J. J. (1982). Case-control studies: Design, conduct, analysis. Oxford University Press. #>  #> IARC classic: Breslow, N. E., & Day, N. E. (1980). Statistical methods in cancer research: Volume I - The analysis of case-control studies. IARC Scientific Publications No. 32. #>  #> For individually matched designs (not the formula implemented here): Dupont, W. D. (1988). Power calculations for matched case-control studies. Biometrics, 44(4), 1157-1168; see the caseControlMatched design. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Oral contraceptive use ischaemic stroke young women, individually matched 1:1 age; control exposure rate 30%, = 2.0. Formula (Dupont discordant-pairs): \[n_{pairs} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\psi} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{\psi-\delta^2}\right]^2}{\delta^2}, \quad \psi = p_1(1-p_0)+p_0(1-p_1)\] Dupont (1988), Biometrics 44(4), 1157-1168. Output: 144 pairs (288 total).
code: res_3_4 <- calculate("caseControlMatched", p0 = 0.30, OR = 2.0, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_3_4) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Individually matched case-control (1:1)" #> • Total sample size: 288 #> • Cases needed: 144 #> • Controls needed: 144 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p0 = control-group exposure rate #> • OR = odds ratio to detect (p1 derived from p0 and OR) #> • psi = expected discordant-pair proportion (pi10 + pi01 = p1*(1-p0) + #> p0*(1-p1)) #> • note = individually matched designs require discordant-pair proportions #> (psi), NOT the discordant odds ratio #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = [Za*sqrt(psi) + Zb*sqrt(psi-delta^2)]^2/delta^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{pairs} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\psi} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{\psi-\delta^2}\right]^2}{\delta^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Matched case-control parameters: control exposure p0 = 0.30, Odds #> Ratio OR = 2 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Case exposure rate: p1 = (OR * p0) / (1 - p0 + OR * p0) = 0.4615. #> • Step 3: Discordant pair probability: psi = pi10 + pi01 = 0.4846; difference #> delta = |pi10 - pi01| = 0.1615. #> • Step 4: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 5: Apply Dupont/Connor formula: n_pairs = [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(psi) + #> Z_beta*sqrt(psi - delta^2)]^2 / delta^2 = 143.38. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: Pairs needed = 144 (Cases = 144, Controls = #> 144). #> Reference: #> Primary: Dupont, W. D. (1988). Power calculations for matched case-control studies. Biometrics, 44(4), 1157-1168. #>  #>  Also: Schlesselman, J. J. (1982). Case-Control Studies, Oxford University Press (matched-pair approximation, p.174); Connor, R. J. (1987). Biometrics, 43(1), 207-211. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: community cross-sectional survey hypertension: prevalence 20% unexposed vs. 30% exposed (obese) participants. Formula: two-proportion kernel 3.1 \(m = 1\) (Machin et al. 2018, Ch. 3). Output: 294 per group, 588 total.

J., Tan, S. B., & Tan, S. H. (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.). Wiley. Chapter 3 (Binary Outcomes). #>  #>  Also: Bhardwaj et al. title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: county diabetes prevalence survey: anticipated prevalence 10%, estimate must lie within \(\pm 2\) percentage points truth 95% confidence. Formula: \[n = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}\] Lwanga & Lemeshow (1991), ; Bhardwaj et al. (2024), p. 2558. Output: 865 participants.
code: res_4_1 <- calculate("singleProportion", p = 0.10, precision = 0.02, alpha = 0.05) print(res_4_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single proportion estimation (precision)" #> • Required sample size: 865 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p = expected proportion (e.g. prevalence) #> • precision = margin of error d (half-width of the CI) #> • confidence level = 95% #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = Z^2 * p(1-p) / d^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify anticipated proportion p = 0.10, margin of error d = 0.02 #> (absolute precision), alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level = #> 95%). #> • Step 3: Compute variance component: p * (1 - p) = 0.10 * 0.90 = 0.09. #> • Step 4: Calculate unrounded sample size: n = Z_(1-alpha/2)^2 * p * (1 - p) / #> d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.09 / (0.02)^2 = 864.33. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Required sample size n = 865. #> Reference: #> Bhardwaj et al. (2024). Determination of sample size for various study designs in medical research: A practical primer. Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care, 13(7), 2555-2561 (p. 2558). #>  #> Also: Lwanga, S. K., & Lemeshow, S. (1991). Sample size determination in health studies: A practical manual. World Health Organization. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Establishing paediatric serum ferritin reference value: population SD = 10 \(\mu\)g/L, mean must estimated within \(\pm 2\) \(\mu\)g/L. Formula: \[n = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2} \cdot \sigma}{d}\right)^2\] Machin et al. (2018), Ch. 9. Output: 97 participants.
code: res_4_2 <- calculate("singleMean", sigma = 10, precision = 2, alpha = 0.05) print(res_4_2) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single mean estimation (precision)" #> • Required sample size: 97 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • sigma = population standard deviation (from pilot/literature) #> • precision = margin of error d #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z * sigma / d)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2} \cdot \sigma}{d}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify population SD sigma = 10, margin of error d = 2, alpha = #> 0.05. #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level = #> 95%). #> • Step 3: Compute unrounded sample size: n = (Z_(1-alpha/2) * sigma / d)^2 = #> (1.96 * 10 / 2)^2 = 96.04. #> • Step 4: Round up to integer: Required sample size n = 97. #> Reference: #> Machin, D., Campbell, M. J., Tan, S. B., & Tan, S. H. (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.). Wiley. Chapter 9. #>  #> Also: Bhardwaj et al. (2024), p. 2558 (continuous outcome precision). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Validating waist circumference proxy body-fat percentage: anticipated \(r = 0.50\), 95% CI half-width must exceed \(\pm 0.10\). Formula (Machin Eqs 19.5-19.8): \[N_{P0} = \frac{4 z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 (1-r^2)^2}{w^2} + 3, \quad N_{Final} = (N_{P0}-3)\left(\frac{w_0}{w}\right)^2 + 3\] Machin et al. (2018), Ch. 19, pp. 307-308 (matches presize::prec_cor). Output: 219 participants (matches presize::prec_cor).
code: res_4_3 <- calculate("singleCorrelation", r = 0.50, precision = 0.10, alpha = 0.05) print(res_4_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single correlation estimation (Fisher z precision)" #> • Required sample size: 219 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • r = anticipated correlation coefficient #> • precision = margin of error d (CI half-width, w = 2*d) #> • confidence level = 95% #> Formula (plain text): #> `Machin 19.5-19.8: N_P0 = 4*z^2*(1-r^2)^2/w^2 + 3, refined via Fisher z bounds` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$N_{P0} = \frac{4 z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 (1-r^2)^2}{w^2} + 3, \quad N_{Final} = (N_{P0}-3)\left(\frac{w_0}{w}\right)^2 + 3$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify anticipated correlation r = 0.50, CI half-width d = 0.10 #> (width w = 2d = 0.20), alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96. #> • Step 3: Machin initial estimate: N_P0 = 4 * Z^2 * (1 - r^2)^2 / w^2 + 3 = #> 219.08. #> • Step 4: Refine via Fisher z transformation limits to adjust for confidence #> interval skewness. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Required sample size n = 219. #> Reference: #> Primary: Machin, D., Campbell, M. J., Tan, S. B., & Tan, S. H. (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.). Wiley. Chapter 19 (The Correlation Coefficient), Equations 19.5-19.8, pp. 307-308. #>  #>  Also: Fisher, R. A. (1921). On the 'probable error' of a coefficient of correlation deduced from a small sample. Metron, 1, 3-32. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Validating colorectal cancer screening kit: expected sensitivity 85%, CI half-width \(\pm 5\%\), clinic prevalence 20%. many confirmed cases many total screens? Formula (Zhou Eq 6.2): \[n_{cases} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}, \quad N_{screen} = \frac{n_{cases}}{\text{prevalence}}\] Zhou, Obuchowski & McClish (2011), Section 6.1.1, pp. 194-196. Output: 196 confirmed cases required; 980 total screened patients.
code: res_5_1 <- calculate("diagAccuracy", "estimate", "proportion", prob = 0.85, d = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20, alpha = 0.05) print(res_5_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Diagnostic accuracy (single)" #> • Cases needed: 196 #> • Total subjects to screen: 980 #> • Total subjects: 980 #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2)^2 * P*(1-P)/d^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{{{cases}}} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify diagnostic accuracy prob (Se or Sp) = 0.85, margin of error d #> = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 (alpha = 0.05). #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level = #> 95%). #> • Step 3: Calculate target cases required: n_cases = Z_sum^2 * prob * (1 - #> prob) / d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.85 * 0.15 / (0.05)^2 = 195.91. #> • Step 4: Adjust for disease prevalence: total subjects to screen = n_cases / #> prevalence = 195.91 / 0.20 = 979.57. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target cases needed = 196, Total subjects to #> screen = 980. #> Reference: #> Primary: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36. #>  #> Review: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: AI lung-nodule system must demonstrate sensitivity significantly 70% industry pass mark; anticipated sensitivity 85%, prevalence 20%. Formula (Hajian-Tilaki Eq 6.8): \[n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha}\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p(1-p)}\right]^2}{(p - p_0)^2}\] Output: 50 cases, 250 screened.
code: res_5_2 <- calculate("diagAccuracy", "test", "proportion", prob = 0.85, p0 = 0.70, prevalence = 0.20, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_5_2) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Diagnostic superiority (single)" #> • Cases needed: 50 #> • Total subjects to screen: 248 #> • Total subjects: 248 #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = [Za*sqrt(P0*Q0) + Zb*sqrt(P*Q)]^2 / (P-P0)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha}\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p(1-p)}\right]^2}{(p - p_0)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Diagnostic superiority (single). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: prob = 0.85, p0 = 0.70, prevalence = 0.20, alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80, method = asymptotic. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: N_cases = [Za*sqrt(P0*Q0) + Zb*sqrt(P*Q)]^2 / #> (P-P0)^2. #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Cases needed: 50; Total subjects to #> screen: 248. #> Reference: #> Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbi.2014.02.013 #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: AI validation, small sample normal approximation unsafe; exact binomial method removes approximation error. Formula: exact binomial — \(P(X \ge r \mid p_0) \le \alpha\), \(P(X \ge r \mid p) \ge 1-\beta\) (’Hern 2001). Output: 49 confirmed cases, critical cutoff \(r = 40\).
code: res_5_3 <- calculate("diagAccuracy", "test", "proportion", prob = 0.85, p0 = 0.70, prevalence = 0.20, method = "exact", alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_5_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Diagnostic superiority (single test, exact binomial)" #> • Cases needed: 49 #> • Total subjects to screen: 245 #> • Total subjects: 245 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • prob = expected diagnostic sensitivity/specificity #> • p0 = unacceptable/null sensitivity or specificity threshold #> • critical_successes = declare superior if correct cases >= 40 of 49 #> Formula (plain text): #> `exact binomial: P(X >= r | p0) <= alpha and P(X >= r | prob) >= power` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$P(X \ge r \mid p_0) \le \alpha \quad \text{and} \quad P(X \ge r \mid p) \ge 1-\beta$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Diagnostic superiority (single test, exact #> binomial). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: prob = 0.85, p0 = 0.70, prevalence = 0.20, alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80, method = exact. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: exact binomial: P(X >= r | p0) <= alpha and P(X #> >= r | prob) >= power. #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Cases needed: 49; Total subjects to #> screen: 245. #> Reference: #> Primary (exact binomial): A'Hern, R. P. (2001). Single stage and double sampling phase II trials. British Journal of Cancer, 85(2), 223-226. #>  #>  Also: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: new breast-lesion AI must improve sensitivity (80% \(\\) 90%) specificity (75% \(\\) 85%) biopsy truth, prevalence 40%. endpoint powered 90% joint power ~80% (Akoglu 2022). what: 5.6 Paired Comparison of Two Diagnostic Tests (Connor Kernel)
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: patients undergo assays (paired design): sensitivities 85% vs. 75%, expected discordant-pair proportion \(\psi = 0.10\) — dramatically fewer cases needed. Formula (Connor): \[n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\psi} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{\psi-\delta^2}\right]^2}{\delta^2}\] Output: 77 pairs cases, 385 screened.
code: res_5_6 <- calculate("diagAccuracyCompare", "test", "proportion", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.75, prevalence = 0.20, paired = TRUE, psi = 0.10, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_5_6) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two diagnostic measures (paired, Connor)" #> • Pairs needed: 77 #> • Total subjects to screen: 381 #> • Cases needed: 77 #> • Total subjects: 381 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p1/p2 = expected sensitivities of the two tests #> • psi = expected discordant-pair proportion (pi10 + pi01) #> • output is in PAIRS (cases); screening total = pairs/prevalence #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = [Za*sqrt(psi) + Zb*sqrt(psi-delta^2)]^2/delta^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\psi} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{\psi-\delta^2}\right]^2}{\delta^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Paired binary parameters: p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.75, discordant pair #> proportion psi = 0.10, difference delta = |p1 - p2| = 0.10. #> • Step 2: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 3: Connor formula: n_pairs = [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(psi) + Z_beta*sqrt(psi - #> delta^2)]^2 / delta^2 = 76.09. #> • Step 4: Round up to integer: Pairs needed = 77. #> Reference: #> Primary: Connor, R. J. (1987). Biometrics, 43(1), 207-211. #>  #>  Also: Akoglu, H. (2022). Turkish Journal of Emergency Medicine, 22(4), Table 2 Eq 3b + Tables 6A/6B; Zhou et al. what: 5.9 ROC Area Under the Curve (AUC) Precision (Binormal Model)
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Planning biomarker validation cohort: anticipated AUC = 0.80, 95% CI half-width \(\pm 0.10\), cases:controls 1:1. Formula (Obuchowski 1994 binormal variance, Zhou Eq 6.5): \[n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC), \quad V = 0.0099\,e^{-^2/2}\left[(5a^2+8) + \frac{^2+8}{R}\right],\ = \sqrt{2}\,\Phi^{-1}()\] Output: 46 cases, 46 controls (92 total).
code: res_5_9 <- calculate("diagAUC", "estimate", "auc", auc = 0.80, d = 0.10, ratio = 1, var_method = "binormal", alpha = 0.05) print(res_5_9) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision" #> • Cases needed: 46 #> • Total subjects to screen: 92 #> • Total subjects: 92 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve #> • precision = desired CI half-width L #> • ratio = case:control ratio R (cases:non-cases; default 1) #> • var_method = binormal variance function #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2 / d)^2 * V(AUC)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC)$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Anticipated AUC = 0.80, precision d = 0.10, supplied allocation R = #> 1, alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 2: Use the binormal variance model with the supplied allocation: V(AUC) #> = 0.1195. #> • Step 3: Calculate cases: n_cases = (Z_(1-alpha/2)/d)^2 * V(AUC) = #> (1.96/0.10)^2 * 0.1195 = 45.89. #> • Step 4: Convert using the supplied allocation: total = n_cases*(1+R) = #> 45.89*(1+1) = 91.78. #> • Step 5: Round up: Target cases needed = 46, Total subjects to screen = 92. #> Reference: #> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.1.2, pp. 196-199 (Eq 6.4/6.5/6.6; CTC worked example). #>  #>  Original variance: Hanley, J. text: Clinical scenario: average, screening 980 patients yields 196 confirmed cases needed Section 5.1 — holds 50% probability. guarantee enough cases 90% probability, inflate screening list. Formula: \[P(\text{Binomial}(N, \text{prevalence}) \ge n) \ge 1-\beta\] Zhou et al. (2011), Eq 6.3. Output: 1058 screened patients guarantee \(\ge 196\) cases 90% probability.
code: safe_n <- screen_required(n = 196, prevalence = 0.20, beta = 0.10) cat("Average screening target: 980; 90% guaranteed enrollment target:", safe_n, "\n") #> Average screening target: 980; 90% guaranteed enrollment target: 1061

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: mammography study 8 radiologists independently read 50 cases two imaging techniques; detect AUC difference 0.10 using Obuchowski-Rockette mixed model. Formula (non-central \(F\), Zhou Eq 6.32): \[\lambda = \frac{J\delta^2}{2\left[\sigma_b^2(1-\rho_1) + \sigma_w^2/Q + \frac{\sigma_c^2(1-\rho_1)}{n} + \rho_2\sigma_b^2\left((1-\rho_1)+(J-1)(\rho_2-\rho_3)\right)\right]}, \quad \text{power} = P(F_{1,J-1}(\lambda) > F_{1-\alpha})\] Zhou et al. (2011), Section 6.5, p. 225. Output: 88.8% statistical power (textbook reports ~89%).
code: res_5_16 <- mrmc_power(n = 50, J = 8, delta = 0.10, sigma_b2 = 0.00123, sigma_w2 = 0.00087, sigma_c2 = 0.05, rho1 = 0.25, rho2 = 0.20, rho3 = 0.10) print(res_5_16) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "MRMC (paired-patient, paired-reader, Obuchowski-Rockette)" #> Parameter roles #>  #> • n = cases per test (paired-patient: total cases) #> • J = readers per test #> • delta = accuracy difference to detect #> • sigma_b2/sigma_w2/sigma_c2 = reader/occasion/case variance components #> • rho1/rho2/rho3 = correlations (same-reader-diff-test / diff-reader-same-test #> / diff-reader-diff-test) #> ! MRMC power depends on 6 variance/correlation components estimated from #> ! pilot data or literature (Zhou Table 6.3); treat results as approximate. #> ! For reader variability planning: sigma_b2 = (accuracy range / 4)^2 is a #> ! common heuristic (Zhou p. 223, Beam 1996 mammography example). #>  #> Formula (plain text): #> `lambda = J*delta^2/(2*[sb2(1-r1) + sw2/Q + sc2(1-r1)/n + #> r2*sb2*((1-r1)+(J-1)(r2-r3))]); power = P(F_{1,J-1}(lambda) > F_{1-alpha})` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$\lambda = \frac{J \cdot \delta^2}{2\left[\sigma_b^2(1-r_1) + \frac{\sigma_w^2}{Q} + \frac{\sigma_c^2(1-r_1)}{n} + r_2 \sigma_b^2((1-r_1)+(J-1)(r_2-r_3))\right]}, \quad \text{Power} = P(F_{1,J-1}(\lambda) > F_{1-\alpha})$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: MRMC (paired-patient, paired-reader, #> Obuchowski-Rockette). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: n = 50, J = 8, delta = 0.10, sigma_b2 = 0.0012, #> sigma_w2 = 0.0009, sigma_c2 = 0.05, rho1 = 0.25, rho2 = 0.20, rho3 = 0.10, #> alpha = 0.05, n_repeats = 1, noncentrality_lambda = 13.7969. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: lambda = J*delta^2/(2*[sb2(1-r1) + sw2/Q + #> sc2(1-r1)/n + r2*sb2*((1-r1)+(J-1)(r2-r3))]); power = P(F_{1,J-1}(lambda) > #> F_{1-alpha}). #> Reference: #> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.5, Eq 6.32, Tables 6.3-6.5, pp. 220-226 (mammography worked example). #>  #>  Model: Obuchowski, N. A., & Rockette, H. E. (1995). Hypothesis testing of diagnostic accuracy for multiple readers, multiple tests. Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation, 24, 285-308. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: ICUs (patients) randomized new catheter-care bundle: complication score 10 \(\\) 12, SD = 3, average 20 beds per ICU, intra-cluster correlation ICC = 0.05. Formula (design effect): \[DE = 1 + (m-1) \times ICC = 1.95, \quad n_{clusters} = \left\lceil \frac{n_{individual} \times DE}{m} \right\rceil\] Donner & Klar (2000); Machin et al. (2018), Ch. 12. Output: 4 clusters (80 patients) per arm, 8 clusters (160 patients) total.
code: res_6_1 <- calculate("clusterRCT", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3, icc = 0.05, cluster_size = 20, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_6_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cluster RCT: Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 80 #> • Total sample size: 160 #> • Clusters per arm: 4 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • icc = 0.05, cluster_size = 20 -> DE = 1.95; n_clusters per arm = 4 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Compute individual-level sample size without clustering from standard #> two-group formulas. #> • Step 2: Calculate design effect (inflation factor): DE = 1 + (cluster_size - #> 1) * ICC = 1 + (20 - 1) * 0.05 = 1.95. #> • Step 3: Inflate sample size for clustering: n_clustered = n_individual * DE. #> • Step 4: Determine clusters required per arm: n_clusters = ceiling(n_clustered #> / cluster_size) = 4. #> • Step 5: Total individuals per arm = 4 * 20 = 80; Total sample size N = 160. #> Reference: #> Primary: Machin, D., Campbell, M. J., Tan, S. B., & Tan, S. H. (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.). Wiley. Chapter 12 (Cluster Designs); Donner, A., & Klar, N. (2000). Design and Analysis of Cluster Randomisation Trials in Health Research. Arnold. #>  #>  Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: 24 counties sequentially adopt hand-hygiene program (6 counties per step, baseline + 4 steps, 100 births per county per period); treatment effect \(\theta = -0.016\) infection risk. Formula (Hussey & Hughes Eq 8): \[Var(\hat{\theta}) = \frac{\tau^2 (\tau^2 + T\sigma^2)}{(IU - W)\tau^2 + (U^2 + ITU - TW - IV)\sigma^2}, \quad \text{power} = \Phi\left(|\theta|/SE - z_{1-\alpha/2}\right)\] Hussey & Hughes (2007), Contemp Clin Trials 28(2), 182-191. Output: 90.8% statistical power.
code: res_6_3 <- calculate("steppedWedge", "test", "mean", theta = -0.016, tau2 = 2.25e-4, sigma2_ind = 0.0475, m = 100, n_clusters = 24, clusters_per_step = 6, alpha = 0.05) print(res_6_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Stepped wedge cluster trial (Hussey-Hughes, mean outcome)" #> • Clusters per arm: 24 #> • Power achieved: 0.908 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • theta = treatment effect (additive scale; e.g. risk difference) #> • tau2 = between-cluster variance (e.g. (CV*mean)^2) #> • sigma2_ind = individual-level variance (binary: p(1-p)) #> • m = individuals sampled per cluster per time point #> • clusters_per_step = clusters randomized at each step (full design) #> ! Hussey & Hughes (2007) Eq 8 assumes no underlying calendar time trends. #> ! If secular time trends are present, statistical power may be lower; #> ! consider incorporating time fixed effects via simulation or swCRTdesign. #>  #> Formula (plain text): #> `Var = I*t2*(t2+T*s2)/((I*U-W)*t2 + (U^2+I*T*U-T*W-I*V)*s2); power = #> Phi(|theta|/se - z)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$\text{Var}(\hat{\theta}) = \frac{I \tau^2(\tau^2+T\sigma^2)}{(IU-W)\tau^2 + (U^2+ITU-TW-IV)\sigma^2}, \quad \sigma^2 = \sigma_{ind}^2/m, \quad \text{Power} = \Phi\left(\frac{|\theta|}{\text{SE}} - z_{1-\alpha/2}\right)$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Stepped wedge cluster trial (Hussey-Hughes, #> mean outcome). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: theta = -0.016, tau2 = 0.0002, sigma2_ind = 0.0475, #> m = 100, n_clusters = 24, clusters_per_step = 6, alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: Var = I*t2*(t2+T*s2)/((I*U-W)*t2 + #> (U^2+I*T*U-T*W-I*V)*s2); power = Phi(|theta|/se - z). #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Clusters per arm: 24; Power achieved: #> 0.908. #> Reference: #> Primary: Hussey, M. A., & Hughes, J. P. (2007). Design and analysis of stepped wedge cluster randomized trials. Contemporary Clinical Trials, 28(2), 182-191 (Eq 8; EPT worked example I=24, T=5). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Knee osteoarthritis pain graded mild/moderate/severe expected distribution 20%/50%/30%; new intra-articular therapy anticipated shift odds better category = 1.5. Formula (Whitehead 1993): \[N = \frac{3\,(Z_{\alpha/2}+Z_{\beta})^2}{(\log )^2\,(1-\sum \bar{p}_j^3)}\] Output: 86 per arm, 171 total.
code: res_6_4 <- calculate("twoOrdinal", "test", "ordinal", or = 1.5, prop_bar = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3), alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_6_4) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two-group ordered categorical outcome (Mann-Whitney / #> proportional odds)" #> • Sample size per group: 86 #> • Total sample size: 171 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • or = anticipated odds ratio (proportional odds) #> • prop_bar = anticipated average category proportions (sums to 1) #> • output: total N and per-group n (equal allocation) #> Formula (plain text): #> `N = 3(Za/2+Zb)^2 / ((log OR)^2 * (1 - sum(p_bar^3)))` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$N = \frac{3\,(Z_{\alpha/2}+Z_{\beta})^2}{(\log OR)^2\,(1-\sum \bar{p}_j^3)}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify odds ratio OR = 1.50, pooled proportion categories = [0.20, #> 0.50, 0.30]. #> • Step 2: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 3: Compute Whitehead variance factor: 1 - sum(p_bar_j^3). #> • Step 4: Whitehead formula: N = 3 * (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [(ln OR)^2 * (1 #> - sum(p_bar^3))]. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Total sample size N = 171, per group n = 86. #> Reference: #> Primary: Whitehead, J. (1993). Sample size calculations for ordered categorical data. Statistics in Medicine, 12(24), 2257-2271. #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Chapter 4 (Ordered Categorical Outcomes). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

what: 6.5 Clinical Prediction Model Development (Riley 2020 BMJ Binary)
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: Developing ICU mortality prediction model 10 candidate predictors, outcome proportion 30%, anticipated Cox-Snell \(R^2_{CS} = 0.10\), target shrinkage \(S = 0.90\). Formula (Riley 2020, criteria B1 & B3): \[n_{B1} = \left(\frac{z}{\delta}\right)^2 \phi(1-\phi), \quad n_{B3} = \frac{P}{(S-1)\ln(1-R^2_{CS}/S)}, \quad n = \max(n_{B1}, n_{B3})\] Riley et al. (2020), BMJ 368, m441 (matches pmsampsize). Output: 850 participants 255 events (matches pmsampsize).
code: res_6_5 <- calculate("predictiveModel", "plan", "binary", prev = 0.30, n_parameters = 10, r2_cs = 0.10, shrinkage = 0.90, precision_delta = 0.05, alpha = 0.05) print(res_6_5) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Prediction model development (Riley 2020, binary)" #> • Required sample size: 850 #> • Events required: 255 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • prev = anticipated outcome proportion in the target population #> • n_parameters = candidate predictor parameters (P) #> • r2_cs = anticipated Cox-Snell R2 (conservative, optimism-adjusted) #> • shrinkage = target uniform shrinkage factor S (default 0.9) #> • mape = target mean absolute prediction error (default 0.05) #> ! B1 (proportion precision, delta=0.050): n = 323 #> ! B3 (shrinkage S=0.90, R2cs=0.1000): n = 850 #> ! B2 (MAPE=0.050, P=10 <= 30): n = 461 (informational) #> ! B4 (optimism in Nagelkerke R2 <= 0.05) is handled inside B3 via the #> ! shrinkage target in the pmsampsize implementation; see Riley 2020 Box 1. #>  #> Formula (plain text): #> `B1: n=(z/d)^2*p(1-p); B3: n=P/((S-1)*ln(1-R2cs/S)); n = max(B1, B3)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{B1} = \left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}}{\delta}\right)^2 \phi(1-\phi), \quad n_{B3} = \frac{p}{(S-1)\ln(1 - R_{CS}^2/S)}, \quad n = \max(n_{B1}, n_{B3})$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Prediction model development (Riley 2020, #> binary). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: prev = 0.30, n_parameters = 10, r2_cs = 0.10, #> max_r2cs = 0.7053, shrinkage = 0.90, mape = 0.05, precision_delta = 0.05, alpha #> = 0.05. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: B1: n=(z/d)^2*p(1-p); B3: #> n=P/((S-1)*ln(1-R2cs/S)); n = max(B1, B3). #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Required sample size: 850; Total #> sample size: 850; Events required: 255. #> Reference: #> Primary: Riley, R. D., Ensor, J., Snell, K. I. E., et al. (2020). Calculating the sample size required for developing a clinical prediction model. BMJ, 368, m441 (Box 1, Figures 1-5). #>  #>  B2 formula: van Smeden, M., et al. (2019). Stat Methods Med Res, 28, 2455-74. B3 derivation: Riley et al. (2019). Stat Med, 38, 1276-96 (PART II). Software: pmsampsize (Stata/R). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

what: 6.9 Inter-Rater Reliability: Two Independent Kappa Test
title: sampleSizeCalc: A Comprehensive Guide to Sample Size Determination in Clinical Research
text: Clinical scenario: new structured reporting checklist improve agreement old one? Anticipated \(\kappa_1 = 0.70\) vs. \(\kappa_2 = 0.50\) two independent reader groups. Formula: \[n = \frac{\left[z_{\alpha}\sqrt{2Q_1} + z_{\beta}\sqrt{Q_1+Q_2}\right]^2}{(K_1-K_2)^2}\] Cantor (1996), Psychological Methods 1(2), 150-153. Output: 214 participants per group.

B. (1996). Sample-size calculations for Cohen's kappa. id: 引言为什么样本量计算是临床研究的第一生命线
what: 引言：为什么样本量计算是临床研究的第一生命线？
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 很多临床医生在申报国家自然科学基金、撰写临床试验方案（Protocol）或提交伦理审查时，最容易被评审专家质疑的就是样本量计算依据。 不经严谨测算就随意定一个样本量（比如“凭经验随访 50 例”），会面临两大致命风险： 1. 样本量过小（Underpowered，检验效能不足）：哪怕药物真有疗效，因为人数太少，微弱的信号会被人体的抽样波动彻底掩盖，最终 \(P > 0.05\)，得出“无统计学显著差异”的假阴性结论，浪费科研经费与受试者心血。 2. 样本量过大（Overpowered，不符合医学伦理）：纳入过多患者不仅拖延试验周期，更在伦理上让多余的受试者暴露在未知疗效或有潜在副作用的试验药物中。 sampleSizeCalc（临床研究样本量计算器）覆盖了现代临床科研从经典双臂 RCT、流行病学调查，到前沿的 Simon 两阶段肿瘤试验、生物等效性（）、多阅片者诊断试验（MRMC）以及 BMJ 最新的 Riley 2020 预测模型样本量规则等 42 个具体场景。 默认打印计算结果时，会同时显示纯文本公式、LaTeX 公式源码、计算过程和参考文献，并按设计提供参数角色说明。 赋值保存结果后，输入对象名称或调用 print() 即可查看；summary() 还会列出全部输入参数及已记录的调整。

id: 统计零基础必读核心概念通俗白话字典
what: 统计零基础必读：核心概念通俗白话字典
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 通俗比喻：“法官冤枉好人的概率”。新药明明没有用，但巧合之下我们误认为新药有用的概率。 常规取值：国际学术界惯例设为 0.05（即 5%）。单侧检验（如非劣效试验）常设为 0.025 或 0.05。 通俗比喻：“警察抓出真凶的把握”。新药确实有用时，我们的试验能以多大的概率把它检测出来。 常规取值：通常设为 0.80（80%） 或 0.90（90%）。把握度要求越高，需要招募的患者越多。 连续型指标：测量出来是具体数值，如收缩压降幅（mmHg）、空腹血糖（mmol/L）。核心参数是“均数差（\(\Delta\)）”与“标准差（\(\sigma\), SD）”。 二分类指标：只有“有效/无效”、“治愈/未治愈”，如有效率 80%、死亡率 15%。 双侧检验：事先不确定新药到底会比对照组好还是差，两头都看（经典临床试验通用）。 单侧检验：只关心新药是否优于对照药，或者新药是否“不差于”对照药（非劣效/优效性试验通用）。 随访中患者失访或退出。设计划脱落率为 \(d\)（如 10%），目标样本量需放大：\(N_{\text{screen}} = \lceil N / (1 - d) \rceil\)。

id: 核心语法统一三轴入口-calculate
what: 核心语法：统一三轴入口 calculate()
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 在 sampleSizeCalc 中，所有计算统一汇聚为一个函数： \[\Large \texttt{calculate(design, task, outcome, ...)}\] 第一轴 design（设计类型）：我们在做什么类型的研究？（"rct", "paired", "cohort", "caseControl", "diagAccuracy", "diagAUC", "singleArmPhaseII", "bioequivalence", "clusterRCT" 等） 第二轴 task（统计任务）：科学目的是什么？（"test" 假设检验, "estimate" 置信区间精度, "noninferiority" 非劣效, "superiority" 优效, "equivalence" 等效） 第三轴 outcome（结局指标）：如何度量疗效？（"mean" 均数, "proportion" 比例, "survival" 生存事件数, "auc" 诊断AUC, "rate" 人时率）

id: 两独立样本均数比较连续变量
previous_headings: 第一章：随机对照试验（RCT）全场景实战
what: 1.1 两独立样本均数比较（连续变量）
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 临床场景：心内科评价新降压药。对照组预计收缩压平均降低 10 mmHg；试验组预计降低 12 mmHg（差值 \(\Delta = 2\) mmHg）。标准差（SD）约为 3 mmHg。设定双侧 \(\alpha = 0.05\)、\(\text{Power} = 80\%\)。 数学公式与出处： \[n = 2 \left( \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2} \right)^2\] 出处：Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. 参数说明：mean1, mean2 为两组均值；sd 为合并标准差（\(>0\)）。 输出解读：每组需 37 人，总计 74 人。计算过程先给出正态近似的每组约 35.32 人，再说明通过 stats::power.t.test() 求解非中心 t 分布效能，最终向上取整为 37 人。
code: res_1_1 <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

id: 两独立样本比例比较二分类治愈率
previous_headings: 第一章：随机对照试验（RCT）全场景实战
what: 1.2 两独立样本比例比较（二分类治愈率）
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 临床场景：消化内科评价幽门螺杆菌根除率。传统 14 天三联方案根除率为 70%（\(p_2 = 0.70\)），新的秘剂四联方案预计达 85%（\(p_1 = 0.85\)）。设定双侧 \(\alpha = 0.05\)、\(\text{Power} = 80\%\)。 数学公式与出处： \[n = \frac{\left[ Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)} \right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}\] 出处：Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, ., & Ury, H. K. (1980). Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. 输出解读：每组需 121 人，总计 242 人。
code: res_1_2 <- calculate("rct", "test", "proportion", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.70, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_2) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent proportions" #> • Sample size per group: 121 #> • Total sample size: 242 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_a/2 * sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_b * sqrt(p1*(1-p1)+p2*(1-p2)))^2 / #> (p1-p2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: p1 = p2 vs H1: p1 != p2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute pooled proportion: p_bar = (p1 + p2) / 2 = (0.85 + 0.70) / 2 #> = 0.775. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute Fleiss formula numerator components: #> Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) = 1.1575; Z_beta*sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) = #> 0.4889. #> • Step 5: Calculate unrounded sample size per group: n = (1.1575 + 0.4889)^2 / #> (0.85 - 0.70)^2 = 120.47. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 121 per group, total sample size N = 242. #> Reference: #> Primary (formula as implemented, without continuity correction): Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, A., & Ury, H. K. (1980). A simple approximation for calculating sample sizes for comparing independent proportions. Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. #>  #> With continuity correction: Casagrande, J. T., Pike, M. C., & Smith, P. G. (1978). An improved approximate formula for calculating sample sizes for comparing two binomial distributions. Biometrics, 34(3), 483-494. #>  #> Book: Fleiss, J. L., Levin, B., & Paik, M. C. (2003). Statistical methods for rates and proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

id: 生存分析与-log-rank-检验时间-事件结局
previous_headings: 第一章：随机对照试验（RCT）全场景实战
what: 1.3 生存分析与 Log-Rank 检验（时间-事件结局）
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 临床场景：晚期非小细胞肺癌一线免疫治疗 vs 化疗的 III 期试验：预期风险比（Hazard Ratio）\(\text{HR} = 0.70\)，试验组与对照组 1:1 分组，检验效能 80%。需累计多少终点事件？ 数学公式与出处： \[E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1 - p_E) [\ln(HR)]^2}\] 出处：Schoenfeld, D. . (1983). Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. 输出解读：试验需随访至累计发生 247 例终点事件（死亡/复发）。
code: res_1_3 <- calculate("rct", "test", "survival", hr = 0.70, pE = 0.50, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_1_3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Survival (log-rank)" #> • Events needed: 247 #> Formula (plain text): #> `E = (Z_a/2 + Z_b)^2 / (pE*(1-pE)*log(HR)^2)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State survival parameters: Hazard Ratio HR = 0.70, experimental arm #> allocation pE = 0.50 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute log hazard ratio: ln(HR) = ln(0.70) = -0.3567. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Apply Schoenfeld formula: E = (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [pE * (1 - #> pE) * (ln HR)^2] = (1.96 + 0.8416)^2 / [0.50 * 0.50 * (-0.3567)^2] = 246.79. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target events needed E = 247. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schoenfeld, D. A. (1983). Sample-size formula for the proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. #>  #> Extensions: #> - Hsieh, F. Y., & Lavori, P. W. (2000). Sample-size calculations for the Cox proportional hazards regression model with nonbinary covariates. Controlled Clinical Trials, 21(6), 552-560. #> - Rubinstein, L. V., Gail, M. H., & Santner, T. J. (1981). Planning the duration of a comparative clinical trial with loss to follow-up and a period of continued observation. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 34(9-10), 469-479. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

what: 1.4 均数非劣效性检验（Non-Inferiority, Mean）
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 临床场景：评价国产仿制降糖药是否不劣于进口原研药：神经病变症状评分（0-30）改善，试验组预期降低 10 分（\(\mu_1 = 10\)），对照组降低 9.5 分（\(\mu_2 = 9.5\)），标准差 \(\text{SD} = 3\)，非劣效界值 \(\text{margin} = 1.0\) 分。 数学公式与出处： \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2\] 出处：Chow et al. (2017) Chapter 4. 单侧 \(\alpha = 0.05\)。 输出解读：每组需 50 人，两组总计 100 人。

C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). what: 2.1 配对均数比较（自身前后对照）
title: sampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 临床场景：哮喘队列：同一批患者吸入糖皮质激素治疗 12 周前后各测一次用力肺活量（FVC），前后差值均数 2 L，差值的标准差 \(\text{SD}_{\text{diff}} = 3\) L。 数学公式与出处： \[n = \left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma_d}{\mu_d}\right)^2\] 出处：Rosner, B. (2015). Fundamentals biostatistics (8th ed.). Cengage Learning. 输出解读：需纳入 20 对受试者（40 人次前后测量）。
code: res_2_1 <- calculate("paired", "test", "mean", meanDiff = 2, sdDiff = 3, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_2_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Paired means" #> • Pairs needed: 20 #> • Total individuals: 40 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = ((Z_a/2 + Z_b) * sd_diff / mean_diff)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma_d}{\mu_d}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State paired difference hypotheses: H0: mu_d = 0 vs H1: mu_d != 0 #> (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Expected paired difference mu_d = 2, SD of differences sigma_d = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Normal approximation: n0 = ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma_d / #> mu_d)^2 = ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = 17.66. #> • Step 5: Exact paired Student's t-test degrees of freedom iteration. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 20 pairs (total individuals = 40). #> Reference: #> Rosner, B. (2015). *Fundamentals of biostatistics* (8th ed.). Cengage Learning. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>
